title: Tone System and Pitch Accent in Standard Ukhrul Tangkhul
alternate_titles: Acoustic Phonetics of Tonal Registers and Tone Sandhi in Tangkhul
journal: Language in India & NEILS Linguistics Bulletin
publisher: Language in India / North East Indian Linguistics Society
subject: Phonetics & Tonology
notes: Pioneering experimental tonological study measuring F0 pitch contours and tone sandhi in Standard Ukhrul Tangkhul.
abstract: This paper investigates the phonetic and phonological properties of the tone system of Standard Ukhrul Tangkhul. While early missionary grammars treated Tangkhul as non-tonal or merely noted pitch variation, instrumental F0 analysis of monosyllabic minimal triplets reveals three distinct contrastive lexical tones: Tone 1 (High Level, 55), Tone 2 (Mid Level, 33), and Tone 3 (Low Falling, 21). We examine tone perturbation caused by syllable-final consonants and document tone sandhi processes occurring in nominal compounding and verbal suffixation.

sections.title: 1. Lexical Tone Contrasts: Minimal Triplets
sections.content: The existence of tone in Tangkhul is conclusively demonstrated by numerous minimal triplets where segmental phonemes are identical but pitch contour differentiates semantic meaning. For instance, the monosyllabic frame /thang/ carries three distinct lexical meanings depending on whether it is uttered with High (55), Mid (33), or Low (21) pitch.

sections.title: 2. Tonal Acoustic Measurements & F0 Contours
sections.content: Pitch contours were tracked across 10 native speakers (5 male, 5 female). Tone 1 exhibits a sustained flat high contour occupying the upper 20% of the speaker's vocal range. Tone 2 runs smoothly along the middle register. Tone 3 exhibits a slight initial rise followed by a steep descent, particularly before pause or sentence boundaries. Sonorant codas carry the pitch contour smoothly, whereas stop codas trigger abrupt glottalization that truncates the contour.

sections.title: 3. Tone Sandhi in Compounding
sections.content: When two monosyllabic words combine into a compound noun, the tone of the second element frequently undergoes sandhi. A Low tone following a High tone is raised to Mid to prevent extreme pitch leaps within a single phonological word. These tone sandhi rules operate systematically across both spoken discourse and traditional musical poetry.

pages.title: 1. Lexical Tone Contrasts: Minimal Triplets
lines: The existence of tone in Tangkhul is conclusively demonstrated by

* thāng (Tone 1: High Level 55) : day, daylight period
* thang (Tone 2: Mid Level 33) : to lift up, raise high
* thàng (Tone 3: Low Falling 21) : knife, machete, dao
